picks.title: USHighPM2.5 daily 1 km ground-level PM2.5
picks.why: Daily gridded total PM2.5 can be aggregated to population-weighted tracts for June 2023.
picks.limitations: Check availability of the actual 2023 files and validation during extreme smoke before analysis; modeled ambient concentration is not personal exposure.

resolution.label: unknown
resolution.reason: 1 km data; set a needed resolution to compare

picks.title: Decennial Census 2020
picks.why: Block population counts support within-tract weighting of gridded PM2.5.
picks.limitations: 2020 counts precede the study and do not capture 2023 population shifts or daily mobility.

resolution.label: good
resolution.reason: Reported by block, finer than your tract unit

picks.title: TIGER/Line and cartographic boundary files
picks.why: Use 2020 tract and block boundaries for aggregation and joining asthma records.
picks.limitations: Select the correct 2020 geography and track boundary changes.

picks.title: EPA Air Quality System (AirData)
picks.why: Daily monitoring observations provide a check on modeled PM2.5 during the smoke episode.
picks.limitations: Monitor locations are sparse and some do not measure every day; independent validation requires checking model inputs.

resolution.label: good
resolution.reason: Reported by address or point, finer than your tract unit

picks.title: NOAA Hazard Mapping System smoke and fire
picks.why: Smoke polygons help contextualize the episode.
picks.limitations: Smoke plume presence alone does not quantify ground-level or smoke-attributable PM2.5.

picks.title: Stanford daily wildfire smoke PM2.5 v2.0 beta
picks.why: Daily smoke-attributable PM2.5 offers a complementary smoke-specific exposure metric through 2023.
picks.limitations: Beta 10 km estimates are coarse for tracts and should not be mistaken for total ambient PM2.5.

resolution.label: unknown
resolution.reason: 10 km data; set a needed resolution to compare

methods.name: Population-weighted spatial aggregation
methods.why: Intersect 2020 blocks, tracts and daily PM2.5 grid cells; calculate weighted daily tract means in µg/m³.
methods.tools: QGIS or Python geopandas, rasterio and pandas

methods.name: Monitor comparison and sensitivity analysis
methods.why: Compare same-day predictions with AQS observations, check smoke peaks and assess sensitivity to grid resolution and population weighting.

methods.name: Asthma analysis design
methods.why: Link tract-day estimates to de-identified events, consider lags, weather, seasonality and confounding, and avoid causal claims from exposure mapping alone.
methods.tools: R or Python; consult Yale epidemiology and privacy experts

next_steps: Confirm access to actual June 2023 daily 1 km files and their model validation before calculating estimates.
Generate tract-day estimates and quantify missingness and uncertainty.
Align asthma outcome dates and residential tract vintage; obtain necessary approvals.
